entities.summary: Evagrius of Antioch was a claimant to the See of Antioch from 388 to 392 CE, succeeding Paulinus and having the support of the Eustathian party. He was a rival to Flavian during the Meletian schism, a theological dispute that lasted from 350 to 451 CE. Evagrius's tenure was marked by his efforts to consolidate his power and establish a stable ecclesiastical order in the region. He was a significant figure in the development of the Antiochene school of theology, which emphasized the importance of tradition and apostolic succession. Evagrius's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his views on the nature of the Church and its governance influenced the development of Eastern Orthodoxy. The Meletian schism, in which Evagrius played a key role, had far-reaching consequences for the theological and ecclesiastical landscape of the Eastern Roman Empire. Evagrius of Antioch's impact on the history of Christianity can be seen in the many churches and monasteries he founded during his reign, including the famous Church of St. John the Theologian in Antioch. The legacy of Evagrius of Antioch is a testament to the enduring power of faith and tradition in shaping the course of human history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Evagrius of Antioch was a significant figure in the development of the Antiochene school of theology and the Eastern Orthodox Church, and his legacy extends beyond his own lifetime to influence the theological and ecclesiastical landscape of the Eastern Roman Empire.
